Frequently asked questions

AVORA recommendations provide decision support. Disconnect power before risky work involving electricity, pumps, valves or plant health, and consult a specialist when necessary.
What should I do when using AVORA for the first time?

First verify garden information and units in Settings. Then check the sensor and season status of each zone in My Plants. A current Raspberry Pi, ESP32 and sensor status in Device Health is enough for a safe start.
What do healthy, attention and no-data statuses mean?

Healthy means sensor data is current and moisture is within range. Attention means moisture or another condition needs follow-up. No data means the sensor is off, has not measured yet or its data is stale.
Why does automatic irrigation not start?

The system and automatic irrigation must be enabled, as must zone irrigation for the relevant zone. Sensor data must be current and stable, cooldown must be complete and a physical valve must be ready. AVORA never runs the pump when a safety condition is missing.
Why is it waiting even though moisture is low?

After irrigation, AVORA waits for water to spread through the root zone. If moisture remains low, it checks the restart difference and cycle limit. This protection prevents unnecessary consecutive irrigation.
How do I test the pump or a valve manually?
Open Manual Watering from Settings > Irrigation Settings. Choose a physical zone and set the duration; the valve and pump run in the safe order.
What is the difference between the four AI tools?

AI Plant Assistant evaluates photos, symptoms, sensor and weather data together. AI Seedling Assistant tracks seedling batches, growth stages and NodeMCU sensors. AI Fertilizer Assistant creates recommendations and plans based on growth stage, application history, stock and product labels. AI Irrigation Assistant monitors moisture behavior and irrigation history.
Does AI Plant Assistant work remotely?

Yes. Your phone and Raspberry Pi do not need the same Wi-Fi when both are connected to Tailscale. The analysis service must be running on the Raspberry Pi; visual analysis is temporarily unavailable if Tailscale disconnects.
Does AI Plant Assistant provide a definitive disease diagnosis?
No. Results provide probability and observation support. Better photos, symptoms and garden data improve confidence; consult an agronomist for serious or progressing conditions.
Which records are added to Plant Journal automatically?
Irrigation, recorded fertilizer applications, AI analyses and certain system events are linked automatically to the relevant zone timeline. You can also add observations, events and growth photos.
How do I view information from a previous season?
Open the zone from My Plants and use the season selector in the journal header. After season closure, irrigation, fertilizer, photo, issue and result summaries remain under the previous year.
Does a fertilizer recommendation mean it was applied?

No. AVORA never applies fertilizer automatically. Review the recommendation and use Mark as Applied only after the application was actually completed. The next date and stock are calculated from this real record.
What happens if Raspberry Pi is on but sensors are offline?

Raspberry Pi and ESP32/sensor connections are monitored separately. The ESP32 can lose power while Raspberry Pi keeps running. The system then remains online but waits for sensor data and blocks automatic irrigation for safety.
Will I lose my records when I change phones?

Garden data saved in Firebase can be loaded again with your account. Use Backup in Settings to move local preferences. After restoring on the new phone, theme, language and supported settings are reapplied.
